gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-thai-lo: Noto Sans Thai Looped reads tall and sturdy, with gaps left open at the curve ends. Disorder is at its best being raw and loud with spaced-out, rod-straight strokes, while the body font does its best work staying quiet and legible in a plain sans way.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-tifinag: Raw energy leads here, courtesy of Disorder and its widely spaced glyphs. Noto Sans Tifinagh does the opposite job, with rounded, inflated lowercase bowls that fill the line, while the heading is best at flat, blunt shouting.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Chaotic and blocky, with Disorder drawing everything in one thick line. Noto Sans Tirhuta then settles the page down, its tall x-height and cut-back terminals leaving big gaps that keep a long run of text moving easily.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-ugariti: Disorder looks rough and scrawled, every stroke a flat, unmodulated line with big lowercase. And Noto Sans Ugaritic, approachable and tight between x-height and caps, reads smoothly across a long passage thanks to open mouths like unjoined chalk arcs.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-vai: Chaotic is the first word for Disorder, its lines traced as if with one marker tip. Noto Sans Vai brings what the heading lacks, words that settle into solid blocks with generous space between curve ends and stems.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-vithkuq: Disorder's lowercase is huge and its glyphs are spaced far apart, so every word looks shouted. Noto Sans Vithkuqi takes the opposite approach beneath it, with a minimal step from capitals to lowercase and open throats that keep the text easy to follow.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Disorder draws every stroke end as if cut from one ribbon, with no swelling anywhere. Noto Sans Wancho follows with a hulking lowercase, like thick chalk pressed hard, so the two feel rough and solid together.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-warang-: Raw and unruly, Disorder holds one marker-like line weight with big, widely spaced lowercase. Noto Sans Warang Citi is best at tidy, solid word blocks.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-yi: Noto Sans Yi reads with a deep midsection in the lowercase, and its rounds stay unsealed like an unlatched hook. Over a long stretch it feels modern and steady.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-zanabaz: Noto Sans Zanabazar Square is approachable, with a soaring x-height and wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp. Disorder, meanwhile, adds a raw, chaotic look above it, like tracing one thick thread, and Noto Sans Zanabazar Square keeps the text open beneath.
